name: DROP
intro: DROP 是报告集中常见的阅读理解 benchmark，强调在段落问答中进行离散推理与数值计算。
build_method: Wikipedia筛选, 对抗式众包, 多答案验证
build_method_en: Wikipedia curation, adversarial crowdsourcing, multi-answer validation
intro_en: DROP is a common reading-comprehension benchmark in the reports, emphasizing discrete reasoning and numerical computation over passages.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:1903.00161v2, the original DROP release ZIP (SHA256 39d2278a29fd729de301b111a45f434c24834f40df8f4ff116d864589e3249d6), and the released AllenNLP v0.9.0 scorer at 052353ed62e3a54fd7b39a660e65fc5dd2f91c7d. DROP selects about 7,000 narrative or number-rich Wikipedia passages, especially NFL summaries, history, and passages with at least 20 numbers. AMT workers receive five random passages, write at least 12 QA pairs using five discrete-reasoning categories, and may submit only questions that a live BiDAF reader misses. Answers are passage/question spans, dates, or numbers with explicit units. The collected QA pool is split by passage into 77,409/9,536/9,622 questions and 5,565/582/588 passages; Dev/Test then receive at least two extra answers and 0.7% invalid items are removed before the final 96,567-question, 6,735-passage release. Version boundary: the paper describes greedy one-to-one multi-span alignment, while the released scorer implements optimal Hungarian alignment; both use normalized EM, numeracy-aware macro F1, and a maximum over gold answers.
